transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
I just don’t see things getting better anymore, no matter what I do. I feel completely stuck, and a colleague at a workshop I do suggested I should come in and talk to someone.
Did these feelings start after a specific stressful event or change in your life, and have they been present most days for more than two weeks?

It all started a little over two years ago when the construction market slowed down and I decided to open my own furniture studio, which brought on a lot of financial stress. This low, stuck feeling has been with me pretty much nonstop ever since, so it's been way longer than just a couple of weeks.
When you feel low and stuck, do you also spend a lot of time worrying or feeling on edge about many different things, or is it more that you’ve lost interest and enjoyment in things you used to like?

It's definitely more about losing interest in things I used to love. While I do worry about the business, the biggest change is that I've stopped enjoying my hobbies like playing guitar, visiting museums, or hiking along the Palisades. I've just been skipping them entirely because I don't have the heart for them anymore.
Have you had any thoughts that life is not worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?
No, I haven't had any thoughts of hurting myself or ending my life. Even though I feel incredibly stuck and hopeless about the future, it has never gotten to that point.
Over the past two years, have you also had low energy, poor concentration, changes in sleep or appetite, or feelings of low self-worth most days?

Yes, I've definitely struggled with low energy and feeling worthless for the last two years. My body constantly feels like it's carrying cinder blocks, and even though I sleep, I still wake up exhausted. I also keep telling myself I'm not good enough and that I'm kidding myself trying to run a studio, though I haven't noticed any major changes in my appetite.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 months during these last two years when you felt back to your usual self, with your mood and interest in things clearly improving?

No, I haven't had any break like that at all. This low, stuck feeling has been pretty much nonstop for the entire two-plus years since I opened the studio. I haven't had any periods where I felt back to my usual self.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 months during these last two years when you felt back to your usual self, with your mood and interest clearly improving?

No, I haven't had any break like that at all. This heavy, stuck feeling has been constant and nonstop for the entire two years since I opened the studio. There hasn't been a single period where I felt back to my usual self.

Over the past two years, have there been days when your mood was so low that you could barely get out of bed or function, or has it been more of a persistent low mood that still lets you keep going day to day?

It's more of a constant, persistent low mood rather than being completely unable to get out of bed. For the past two years, I've been dragging myself through each day to keep the shop going and do basic tasks, but it always feels like I'm carrying a heavy weight. I'm just going through the motions with a lot of extra effort.
Have you ever had a period of at least two months during the past two years when you felt back to your usual self, with your mood and interest in things clearly improving?

No, I really haven't had any break like that. This low, stuck feeling has been constant and pretty much nonstop ever since I opened the studio a little over two years ago. There hasn't been a single time where I felt back to my usual self or felt my mood lift.
Have there been any periods of at least 2 months in the past two years when you felt back to your usual self, with your mood and interest in things clearly improving?

No, I haven't had any breaks like that at all. This heavy, low feeling has been constant and nonstop for the entire two years since I opened the studio, without any real lift or relief. I just haven't felt back to my usual self even for a short time.
During this time, have you had any 2-week period when the depression got clearly worse, with several symptoms becoming strong enough to meet a full major depressive episode?

I don't recall any specific two-week period where things suddenly got much worse or spiked. It has really just been a steady, continuous grayness and low mood that has dragged on at the same constant level for the past two years.

Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks during these two years when your depression became clearly worse, with symptoms like much more severe low mood, loss of interest, sleep or appetite changes, or feeling slowed down or hopeless?

No, there hasn't been any specific two-week stretch where things suddenly got much worse. It’s really just been a steady, constant, heavy gray feeling that has stayed at the same dragging level pretty much nonstop for the entire two years.
Have you ever had any separate period of at least 2 weeks when your depression became much worse, with most of the day feeling very depressed or losing interest in almost everything?

No, I haven't had any separate periods where the depression suddenly spiked or got much worse for a couple of weeks. It has just been a steady, constant, and unchanging heavy feeling that has persisted nonstop for the last two years.
Have you ever had a 2-week period during these past two years when your symptoms became clearly worse, with most of the day feeling very depressed or losing interest in almost everything?

No, I really haven't noticed any specific two-week period where it suddenly got much worse. It has just been a constant, steady, heavy gray feeling that has dragged on nonstop for the entire two years.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when your depression became clearly worse, with most of the day feeling very depressed or losing interest in almost everything?

No, there really hasn't been a distinct two-week block where things suddenly plunged or got much worse. It's just been this constant, heavy gray baseline and a loss of interest in my hobbies, like hiking and guitar, that I've been dragging myself through nonstop for the last two years.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when your depression became clearly worse, with most of the day feeling very depressed or losing interest in almost everything?

No, it really hasn't come in waves or had any specific two-week periods where it suddenly got much worse. It’s just been a constant, steady, and continuous gray feeling that has been dragging me down pretty much nonstop for the entire two years.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks during these two years when your depression clearly became worse, with most of the day feeling very depressed or losing interest in almost everything?

No, I haven't experienced any specific two-week stretch where the depression suddenly spiked or got worse than usual. It has just been a steady, constant, and unchanging heavy, gray feeling that has stayed with me nonstop for the entire two years.
Have you had any changes in your sleep pattern, such as sleeping much more or much less than usual, along with the low mood?

I haven't really noticed a major change in the actual amount of sleep I get. It's just that I feel completely exhausted and worn out all the time, regardless of how many hours of sleep I manage to get.

Have you ever had a separate period of at least 2 weeks during these two years when your depression became clearly worse, with most of the day feeling very depressed or losing interest in almost everything?

No, there hasn't been any separate two-week block where things suddenly got much worse. It's just been this same heavy, gray feeling hanging over me as a steady, constant weight pretty much nonstop for the entire two years.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks, at any point in your life, when you felt depressed or lost interest in almost everything most of the day nearly every day?

Yes, I've definitely experienced that, but it has lasted much longer than just two weeks—it has been a constant, heavy presence for over two years now. During this entire time, I've felt a persistent low mood and have completely lost interest in things I used to love, like playing the guitar, hiking, and visiting museums.
Have you ever had any separate episode in your life, lasting at least 2 weeks, where your depression or loss of interest was clearly worse than usual and met the level of a major depressive episode?

No, I haven't experienced any separate, distinct episodes where the depression got much worse for two weeks or more. It has really just been this same consistent, low, and heavy feeling for the entire past two years.
Have you ever had any separate episode in your life lasting at least 2 weeks where you felt clearly more depressed or lost interest in almost everything, even if it was before these past two years?

No, I don't recall ever having a separate period of depression or losing interest in things before this current struggle started. Before these past two years, I was generally doing fine and enjoying my life.
Have you ever had a period of at least 4 days when you felt unusually energetic or irritable, needed much less sleep, talked more than usual, or did things that were out of character for you?
No, I’ve never experienced anything like that at all. My mood has just been consistently low and heavy, and I always feel worn out rather than energetic.
Have you ever had a separate period of at least 2 weeks in your life when your depression was clearly worse than usual, with most of the day feeling depressed or losing interest in almost everything?

No, I haven't really experienced a separate, distinct two-week period where the depression was suddenly much worse. It has just been a steady, continuous, and unrelenting heavy gray feeling for the entire past two years.
Do you also feel irritable, easily frustrated, or unusually sensitive to criticism most days?
No, I wouldn't say I feel particularly irritable or easily frustrated. It's more that I just feel incredibly tired, down, and hopeless most of the time.
Have you had any medical problems, started any new medications, or increased alcohol or drug use around the time this low mood began?
No, I haven't had any major medical problems or started taking any new medications. I also haven't increased my use of alcohol or drugs since this low mood began.
Did these low mood and loss of interest symptoms first begin before age 21, or did they start later in adulthood?

They definitely started later in adulthood, just a little over two years ago when I was about 43. It began during that slow stretch in the construction market when I first opened my furniture studio. I never experienced any feelings like this when I was younger or before age 21.

Before these symptoms began two years ago, did you ever have a long-standing pattern of feeling mildly depressed or down for most of the day on most days, even if it never got severe enough to be a major episode?
No, I don't recall ever having that kind of long-standing low mood before two years ago. My mood was generally okay and I felt fine before the stress of opening the furniture studio started.
Have your symptoms been present most of the day, more days than not, for at least 2 years without any symptom-free period longer than 2 months?

Yes, that's exactly right. This heavy, low feeling has been with me pretty much nonstop for a little over two years now, ever since I opened my furniture studio. I haven't had any real breaks or periods during this time where I felt better.
